title: Dundee Cake
subtitle: Scottish fruit cake with blanched almonds
excerpt: A rich fruit cake from Dundee made with currants, raisins, orange peel, and whisky, topped with concentric circles of blanched almonds before baking. Lighter and less dense than a Christmas cake.

recipe.sourceNotes: Dundee cake is Scotland's most famous baked good after shortbread. It was first made commercially by the Keiller marmalade company in Dundee in the late 19th century, using the orange peel that was a by-product of their marmalade production. The cake is distinguished from other British fruit cakes by three things: the inclusion of marmalade or orange peel for a distinctive citrus note, the lighter, less dense texture compared to a dark Christmas cake, and the characteristic topping of blanched almonds arranged in concentric circles. It keeps well for two weeks wrapped in foil, and the flavour improves after a day or two as the fruit and alcohol meld together.

recipeTools.notes: A deep 20 cm round cake tin.

content.text: Line the tin with a double layer of baking paper and tie a double layer of newspaper around the outside of the tin: this insulates the edges and prevents the outside from drying out during the long, slow bake. The cake is done when a skewer inserted into the centre comes out clean. If the top is browning too quickly, cover loosely with foil after 45 minutes.

Heat the oven to 160 C / fan 140 C / gas 3. Line a deep 20 cm round tin with a double layer of baking paper. Beat the butter and sugar until pale and fluffy. Add the eggs one at a time, beating well after each.
Fold in the flour, mixed spice, and ground almonds. Fold in the fruits, mixed peel, marmalade, orange zest, and whisky.
Spoon into the prepared tin and level the surface. Arrange the blanched almonds on top in concentric circles, pressing them in lightly.

Bake for 1 hour 30 minutes until a skewer inserted into the centre comes out clean. Leave to cool in the tin for 30 minutes, then transfer to a wire rack. Wrap in foil when fully cold. Keeps for 2 weeks.
